title: Why should anyone care about Evals? — Manu Goyal, Braintrust
talk_summary: This is a short, mostly motivational lightning talk arguing that evals are essential because they let you iterate offline instead of getting signal only from production. It contains no concrete eval methodology, tooling, or measured results, only the high-level claim that evals are a 'laboratory' for experimentation.

takeaways.technique: Offline eval loop as pre-prod signal
takeaways.what_they_do: Build an offline eval suite so most of the product iteration loop happens before shipping, rather than learning from production failures.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If I didn't have evals, the only way I can get any signal on my changes is by shipping it to prod

takeaways.what_they_do: Apply the same metrics offline and on production data so prod examples can be prioritized for the next iteration.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you actually apply the same metrics from offline to your online production data, you now have datadriven signal about which examples in prod are going to be most useful
